newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt says don't choke Internet with regulation.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says don't choke Internet with regulation.

text.p: Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Wednesday Germans should be less apprehensive about the information revolution and urged governments not to choke the Internet with unnecessary regulation.

Speaking on the 25th anniversary of the German-language service of the news and information group Reuters Plc, Rexrodt said an international conference on the information society hosted by Germany would focus on questions of data security and curbing abuse of public communications networks.

"I am certain that we will find a solution to these problems without suffocating the networks in a mass of regulation," he said according to the text of a speech prepared for delivery at a Reuters celebration in Bonn.
"All in all I wish there would be more enthusiasm and less apprehension in Germany about opportunities to communicate in the information society."

The European Union will hold an international conference in Germany next year to discuss the impact on society of the Internet global computer network and new communications technology that are changing the way people work and play.
Rexrodt noted the advance of information through such global networks was also one of the driving forces behind the movement towards democracy in eastern Europe and elsewhere.
"Without the triumphant march of communications technology, the collapse of hard-line Socialism in Europe might possibly have been delayed for decades," he said.

The minister also noted that new technologies and services were creating a huge market that would drive global investment in communications technology worldwide to around 250 billion marks over the next ten years.
"If the conditions are right, a total of 1.5 million jobs could be created here at home over the next 15 years," he said.
